title: How Unix spell ran in 64 kB of RAM
summary: This article explores how the original Unix 'spell' command operated within just 64KB of RAM on early PDP-11 systems, using clever data structures like hashed dictionaries, compressed tries, and compact string storage techniques to perform spell-checking under extreme memory constraints.
problem_solved: How to implement a functional spell-checker that fits in extremely limited memory (64KB) on early computing hardware
why_valuable: Demonstrates timeless software engineering principles for optimizing resource usage that remain relevant for modern embedded systems and memory-constrained environments
